guards.label: self-merge-posture
guards.note: Critical Rule 5 is the single source of truth for whether this repo grants unattended self-merge, and every merge step defers to it. The alternates are anchor substrings taken from the two canonical wordings of that ONE rule: the first anchors the gated wording, the second the withheld wording, and the third is a fragment both skills' withheld wording shares (autonomous-dev-flow and tackle-issues phrase the rest of that sentence differently). None is redundant — dropping any one leaves a legitimate posture unmatched. The guard fires when the rule line is gone, not when a repo picks the other posture. Do NOT relax this to a bare 'Unattended Merge Gate' substring: that phrase also appears in prose about the gate and would pass a file whose rule 5 had been deleted.
anyOf: Merge only through the Unattended Merge Gate
NEVER merge, however clean the PR is
does not grant unattended merge authority

guards.label: explicit-path-staging
guards.note: #163: binds the PROHIBITION LIST, not the rationale. Both alternates require `git add -u` and `git add -A` to be named together as banned. Three earlier alternates were removed because they matched the sentence that EXPLAINS the ban ('`-u` is not the safe one: ...'), which sits on the same physical line — so deleting `git add -u` from the ban list still passed on 4 of 7 templates while the rule was gone. Never anchor on a bare `-u`: it appears in `sort -u`, `git push -u origin`, and the rationale. The two alternates are the same claim with the list order swapped.

guards.label: lfs-filter-failure-mode
guards.note: #163: binds the RATIONALE for banning `-u` specifically — that it restages a tracked file the clean/smudge filter rewrote, turning a binary into an LFS pointer. Alternates 3 and 4 previously matched a bare mention of an LFS filter or pointer anywhere in the file, so an unrelated LFS sentence satisfied the guard with the rationale deleted. They now require `-u` on the same line, which is what makes them rewordings of the same sentence rather than keyword hits.

guards.label: assert-branch-before-write
guards.note: Binds the re-verification rule, not the branch variable. `SESSION_BRANCH` is deliberately NOT an alternate: it appears in the bash blocks, so a guard on it would still pass after the rule sentence was deleted — vacuous. Alternate 2 requires a re-check verb on the same line as the command, so `BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)` (the ordinary one-time read, e.g. create-pr step 1) does not satisfy it; the point of #163 is that reading the branch ONCE is exactly the failure.

guards.label: self-merge-posture
guards.note: Critical Rule 5 is the single source of truth for whether this repo grants unattended self-merge, and every merge step defers to it. The alternates are anchor substrings taken from the two canonical wordings of that ONE rule: the first anchors the gated wording, the second the withheld wording, and the third is a fragment both skills' withheld wording shares (autonomous-dev-flow and tackle-issues phrase the rest of that sentence differently). None is redundant — dropping any one leaves a legitimate posture unmatched. The guard fires when the rule line is gone, not when a repo picks the other posture. Do NOT relax this to a bare 'Unattended Merge Gate' substring: that phrase also appears in prose about the gate and would pass a file whose rule 5 had been deleted.
anyOf: Merge only through the Unattended Merge Gate
NEVER merge, however clean the PR is
does not grant unattended merge authority

guards.label: explicit-path-staging
guards.note: #163: binds the PROHIBITION LIST, not the rationale. Both alternates require `git add -u` and `git add -A` to be named together as banned. Three earlier alternates were removed because they matched the sentence that EXPLAINS the ban ('`-u` is not the safe one: ...'), which sits on the same physical line — so deleting `git add -u` from the ban list still passed on 4 of 7 templates while the rule was gone. Never anchor on a bare `-u`: it appears in `sort -u`, `git push -u origin`, and the rationale. The two alternates are the same claim with the list order swapped.

guards.label: lfs-filter-failure-mode
guards.note: #163: binds the RATIONALE for banning `-u` specifically — that it restages a tracked file the clean/smudge filter rewrote, turning a binary into an LFS pointer. Alternates 3 and 4 previously matched a bare mention of an LFS filter or pointer anywhere in the file, so an unrelated LFS sentence satisfied the guard with the rationale deleted. They now require `-u` on the same line, which is what makes them rewordings of the same sentence rather than keyword hits.

guards.label: assert-branch-before-write
guards.note: Binds the re-verification rule, not the branch variable. `SESSION_BRANCH` is deliberately NOT an alternate: it appears in the bash blocks, so a guard on it would still pass after the rule sentence was deleted — vacuous. Alternate 2 requires a re-check verb on the same line as the command, so `BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)` (the ordinary one-time read, e.g. create-pr step 1) does not satisfy it; the point of #163 is that reading the branch ONCE is exactly the failure.

skills.name: test-plan
skills.description: Walk a codebase, enumerate every testable surface, and emit a structured, code-grounded corpus of test cases — a generator, not a renderer. The output is DATA: a YAML (or JSON) corpus plus a markdown index, sized for a whole repo (~6-10 surface areas, ~100 cases) rather than for one change set. Every case carries a stable id, copy-pasteable prereqs / steps / expected / gotchas, a `safe` or `live` risk tag, shell-aware commands, and at least one `file:line` citation to the code that establishes it. An **executor** consumes the corpus: `/smoke-form` renders the human-visual subset into an interactive HTML pass for a person, while an agent or the test suite runs everything else.

guards.label: never-fabricate-omit-instead
anyOf: an invented command is worse than a missing one

guards.label: file-line-grounding-per-case
anyOf: MUST carry at least one `file:line` grounding entry
must trace back to one of
guards.note: Binds the grounding RULE sentence in section 4, not the `grounding:` field in the schema block or the `grounding` column in the report table — those are the decoration that survives when an agent rewrites the rule.

guards.label: no-backend-cases-to-humans
anyOf: [Nn]ever route a purely back-end case to a human
guards.note: smoke-form's own LIVE/VISUAL-ONLY rule is quoted just above this one as context; the alternates are deliberately worded so the quotation cannot satisfy the guard on its own.

guards.label: emit-data-not-html
anyOf: [Tt]his skill emits data, not a document

guards.label: no-secrets-in-cases
anyOf: [Nn]ever put a real credential in a case

guards.label: safe-vs-live-tagging
guards.note: Binds the FAIL-SAFE DIRECTION, not just the existence of tagging. The rule is one sentence with two clauses — tag every case, and default to `live` on doubt — and the second is the safety-critical half: flipping it to `safe` makes the generator emit live-effect cases as safe. A bare `[Tt]ag every case` alternate stayed green through exactly that inversion, so every alternate now requires the `live`-on-doubt direction.

guards.label: safe-mode-gate
guards.note: Binds the safe-mode GATE, which #107 requires alongside tagging and which the old combined guard did not protect. Anchored on the refusal behaviour, not on the section heading.

guards.label: shell-default-git-bash
guards.note: Binds ONLY the shell DEFAULT — a named #107 requirement. Split from shell-aware-commands, where the labeling alternates kept the guard green when the default was flipped to PowerShell.
anyOf: Default to Git Bash on Windows

guards.label: shell-label-powershell-only
guards.note: Binds ONLY the labeling rule, which is a different requirement from the default shell.

skills.name: tiered-delegation
skills.description: The cost-discipline constitution for multi-agent work: the **session's top model orchestrates; cheaper tiers execute**. Invoke it when a session is about to fan out subagents or workflows (audits, marathons, parallel implementation, large research) to load the delegation rules — who does what tier of work, how far down to push each task, and when a claim must be re-verified before it drives an action. It composes with the marathon machinery (`/prime-directive`, `/tackle-issues`, `/parallel-dev`) and with ad-hoc Workflow/Agent fan-outs alike.

guards.label: no-duplicate-delegated-work
anyOf: waits for the result instead of re-running

guards.label: parallel-writers-get-worktrees
anyOf: write-capable workers each get a worktree

guards.label: effort-dial-before-tier
anyOf: Raising effort is cheaper than raising tier

skills.name: unattended-merge
skills.description: Defines when an autonomous session (e.g. `/autonomous-dev-flow`, `/tackle-issues`) may merge its **own** PR without a human pause, and what record it must leave behind. This replaces the old blanket "never merge — PRs accumulate for user review" rule for unattended sessions: a PR that has genuinely cleared every gate may merge so dependent work isn't deadlocked overnight, but nothing merges on faith and every merge is visible in the session report.

skills.name: visual-brief
skills.description: Generate a polished, **self-contained HTML brief** of a topic — session status, a plan, or a code walkthrough — saved to a durable folder and opened in the browser. Built for moments when a plain chat wall is hard to absorb: context switches, long-running sessions, or understanding how a codebase fits together.

guards.label: respects-reader-colour-scheme
guards.note: #135: the skeleton shipped a hardcoded dark palette with no prefers-color-scheme query, so every brief rendered dark whatever the reader's system setting. Each alternate must match the CSS RULE BLOCK — the query plus its opening brace and :root — not the query string alone. Two earlier versions failed: listing the prose rules as alternates passed when only the query was deleted (anyOf matches ANY one), and matching the bare query still passed because Customization Points quotes '@media (prefers-color-scheme:light)' verbatim in backticks, so the guard matched the documentation instead of the code. Both partial mutants now fail. The two alternates are one claim in its two legitimate spellings: dark default with a light query, or light default with a dark one.

skills.name: weekly-review
skills.description: The **Monday TPM pass over everything on this machine**: scan every repo for the trailing week's git activity, fan out one read-only scan agent per active repo, sweep the quiet tail, aggregate local session usage from the transcripts, and write a dated Markdown note plus a self-contained HTML brief into the vault. The chat message it ends with is **a short list of decisions waiting on the owner and one pointer to the note** — never a recap of the week, which is what the note is for. Reach for it at the top of the week, or any time "what happened across all my projects, and what needs me?" is the actual question.

guards.label: report-only-no-state-changes
guards.note: The review is read-only by construction: a weekly report that mutates the state it describes cannot be trusted the following week. Alternates must match the prohibition sentence itself — never the '## Report-only' heading, which survives deleting the rule beneath it.
anyOf: [Nn]othing in this run merges a PR, pushes a branch
[Nn]ever merge, push, or change issue state during (a|the) review

guards.label: scan-agents-are-read-only
guards.note: The per-repo agents run against the owner's shared working copies, in parallel. A fetch or checkout inside one mutates the state the scan was sent to describe and races every other session in that directory.
anyOf: [Aa] scan agent that fetches or checks out

guards.label: dedup-repos-sharing-a-remote
guards.note: Double-counting a 40-PR series across two working copies of one repo is the single most misleading error this report can make. The rule is the counting instruction, not the CUSTOMIZE bullet listing the known pairs — that bullet is stripped at install time.
anyOf: [Tt]wo directories with the same `origin` remote are one repo

guards.label: automated-sync-waves-are-not-work
guards.note: Fleet-wide skill-registry waves land identical commits in fifteen repos within minutes. Counting them as activity inflates a two-product week into a fifteen-repo week, which is how a status report stops being read.
anyOf: [Aa]n automated skill-registry sync wave is not a week of work
[Aa] repo whose entire diff is (a|an automated) sync wave is [^\n]{0,20}quiet

guards.label: usage-numbers-carry-their-honesty-labels
guards.note: Cache-inclusive input read as fresh spend overstates the week by orders of magnitude, and a wall-clock transcript span read as focused time overstates it again. The label must travel WITH the number, so alternates match the rule sentence rather than the word 'cache-inclusive' wherever it happens to appear.
anyOf: every (one|number) carries its caveat in the same sentence
[Ee]very usage figure ships with its honesty label

guards.label: final-message-leads-with-the-decision-list
guards.note: The owner reads this to find what needs them. Alternates must match the ordering rule, not the '**Needs you**' string in the example block, which survives deleting the rule.
anyOf: [Tt]he final chat message opens with the decision list
[Ll]ead the final message with what needs the owner

guards.label: every-needs-user-item-reaches-the-owner
anyOf: if an item appeared there, it appears here
no open owner decision is dropped between the scan and the message

guards.label: final-message-is-not-a-prose-wall
guards.note: The week is written up twice already (note + HTML). A third telling in chat is the failure mode the skill exists to prevent.
anyOf: [Aa] prose recap in chat is the failure mode this skill exists to prevent
[Tt]he report is the note; the message is the ask
[Nn]ever restate the note.s contents in chat

guards.label: zero-attribution
anyOf: carries AI or agent attribution of any kind
[Nn]o AI attribution in the note, the HTML
[Nn]ever attribute any part of the week to an agent

guards.label: series-number-continues-the-previous-note
guards.note: A second 'Weekly Review #1' silently breaks the series the owner navigates the year by. The rule is 'derive it from the folder', not the mere presence of a `series:` key in the frontmatter example.
anyOf: [Tt]he series number continues the previous note
never restart at #1 because you did not look
[Rr]ead the last note.s series number and add one
